Rashi on Ketubot 8b:10:1.hebrew: בבריתו של אברהם - שגמל חסדים, דכתיב (בראשית כ״א:ל״ג) ״ויטע אשל״, ר"ת של אשל אכילה שתיה לויה:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:10:1.english: In the covenant of Abraham - For he bestowed loving-kindness, as it is written (Genesis 21:33) “And he planted an eshel,” the initials of which [spell] eating, drinking, escorting.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:12:1.hebrew: עשרה כוסות - להרבות לו בשתיה, כדכתיב (משלי ל״א:ו׳) תנו שכר לאובד ויין למרי נפש:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:12:1.english: Ten cups - To give him more to drink, as it is written (Proverbs 31:6): "Give strong drink to him who is perishing, and wine to those of bitter soul."

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:12:2.hebrew: קודם אכילה - שהיו רגילין להמשיך פרפראות לפני סעודה, כגון כיסנין וסופגנין ואיסקריטין, ובאותם פרפראות משקין לאבל ג' כוסות:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:12:2.english: Before eating - For they were accustomed to serve appetizers before the meal, such as kisnin (pastries), sufganin (spongy cakes), and iskritin (flat cakes); and with those appetizers, they would give the mourner three cups to drink.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:12:3.hebrew: אחד כנגד הזן - על כל ברכה שותה הכוס, ומוזגין לו אחר:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:12:3.english: One corresponds to "Who feeds" - For each blessing he drinks the cup, and they pour him another.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:13:1.hebrew: כנגד חזני העיר - תקנו להם ברכה עליו, לפי שהיו שמשי העיר, להתעסק במתים ובשאר צרכי ציבור:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:13:1.english: Corresponding to the attendants of the city - They instituted for them a blessing on it [the cup], because they were the city's attendants, [who] would occupy themselves with the dead and with other communal needs.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:13:2.hebrew: פרנסי העיר - שהיו עשירים מבזבזים ממונם לקבורת עניים:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:13:2.english: The leaders of the city - For they were wealthy people who would spend their money on the burial of the poor.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:13:3.hebrew: כנגד בהמ"ק - תקנו עליו ברכת ניחומים, שינחמנו המקום בבניינו מאבלנו, שאנו מתאבלים עליו כעל מת:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:13:3.english: Corresponding to the Temple - They instituted over it a blessing of consolation, that the Omnipresent should console us with its rebuilding for our mourning, for we mourn over it as over a dead person.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:13:4.english: Corresponding to Rabban Gamliel - [The Gemara] explains below.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:13:5.english: To its former [state] - [That is, to] ten cups.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:14:1.hebrew: הוצאת המת - שהיו קוברים אותו בכלים יקרים, כגון שיראין וסרקות:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:14:1.english: The funeral [expenses] of the deceased - For they would bury him in expensive garments, such as silks and sarkot [fine cloths].

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:14:2.hebrew: בצרדא בר זוזא - בגד קנבוס שאינו שוה אלא דינר:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:14:2.english: In a tzerada worth a zuz - A hemp garment that is worth only one dinar.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:1:1.hebrew: בברכת המזון - להצטרף לג' לזמן עליו, שהרי הוא חייב בכל המצות:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:1:1.english: With regard to Grace after Meals - To join [with others] to make up three for [reciting] the invitation [to Grace] over it, for he is obligated in all the commandments.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:2:1.hebrew: בשורה - כשהיו חוזרין מן הקבר, היו עושין שורה סביב האבל לנחמו, ומושיבין אותו, והן עומדים סביב. ואמרי' בסנהדרין (דף יט.): אין שורה פחות מי':
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:2:1.english: In the line - When they would return from the grave, they would form a line around the mourner to comfort him, and they would seat him while they stood around [him]. And we say in Sanhedrin (19a): A line is no fewer than ten.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:2:2.hebrew: ברחבה - כשמברין את האבל סעודה ראשונה משל אחרים, כדאמרינן במועד קטן (דף כז:) "היו מברין אותו ברחבה", ומברכין שם ברכת אבלים, כדמפרש לקמיה "ברוך מנחם אבלים":
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:2:2.english: In the square - When they feed the mourner the first meal, [provided] from the food of others, as we say in Moed Katan (27b): "They would feed him in the square." And there they recite the blessing of the mourners, as [the Gemara] explains below: "Blessed is He Who comforts mourners."

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:4:1.english: He said to him - [Reish Lakish said] to his disseminator.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:4:2.hebrew: כל קביל ינוקא - לנגד המאורע, אמור דברים של ניחומים על מיתת הילד:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:4:2.english: Opposite the child - In response to the event, [say] words of consolation about the death of the child.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:4:3.english: And the Lord saw - What did the fathers do?

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:4:4.hebrew: וינאץ מכעס - שהכעיסוהו, וגרמו לו לפקוד על בניהם ובנותיהם:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:4:4.english: And He abhorred them, due to the provocation - That they provoked Him, and caused Him to punish their sons and their daughters.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:5:1.hebrew: ואית דאמרי - לא תינוק היה המת, אלא בחור היה, והך קרא אמר "עַל כֵּן על בחוריו וגו'":
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:5:1.english: And there are those who say - The deceased was not a child, but a youth, and this verse says: "Therefore, upon their young men [the Lord shall not rejoice]" etc.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:5:2.hebrew: של ע' שנה - ועוד דריש כמו ״ועד עולמו של אדם״: נטויה, נהפכת מטוב לרע:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:5:2.english: Of seventy years - And he expounds "ve'od" ["still"] as "ve'ad" ["until"], as in "until the world of a person" [i.e., his lifetime]: [His hand is] outstretched — [the decree] is turned from good to evil.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:6:1.hebrew: אתא לנחומי צעורי מצער ליה - בתמיה: מוכיח על פניו שבשביל עונו מת בנו:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:6:1.english: He came to comfort — he distresses him?! - [This is stated] as a question of astonishment: He rebukes him to his face, [implying] that because of his sin his son died.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:6:2.hebrew: חשיב את לאתפוסי אדרא - חשוב אתה למעלה, לתופסך ואת בניך בעון הדור, דקי"ל: בזמן שצדיקים בדור, צדיקים נתפסים על הדור, שנאמר: "וממקדשי תחלו" (יחזקאל ט):
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:6:2.english: You are significant to be seized for the generation - You are considered important Above, such that [God] seizes you and your sons for the sin of the generation, as we hold: When there are righteous people in the generation, the righteous are seized for the [sins of the] generation, as it is stated: "And from My Sanctuary you shall begin" (Ezekiel 9):

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:7:1.hebrew: האל הגדול ברוב גודלו - בברוך פתח בה: ברוך אתה ה' אלהינו מלך העולם, האל הגדול וכו':
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:7:1.english: God, Who is great in the abundance of His greatness - He opened it with a blessing: "Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, the great God," etc.:

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:8:1.hebrew: אחינו המיוגעים כו' - ברכה הסמוכה לחברתה היא, וכן סדורות על הסדר:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:8:1.english: Our brothers, who are exhausted, etc. - It is a blessing that is adjacent to its fellow [blessing], and so they are arranged in order.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:8:2.hebrew: באבל הזה תנו לבבכם לחקור זאת שזאת עומדת לעד - שהכל מתים, ולא תבכו יותר מדאי:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:8:2.english: In this mourning, set your heart to examine this: that this stands forever - For everyone dies, and do not weep excessively.

Rashi on Ketubot 8b:9:1.hebrew: משתה הראשונים לימא - כלומר משתה ראשונים הוא:
Rashi on Ketubot 8b:9:1.english: “The drink of the first” — let him say - [That is,] it is the drink of the first:

Tosafot on Ketubot 8b:1:1.hebrew: כי תניא ההיא בברכת המזון - פי' בקונטרס: להצטרף עם ב' לזימון, שהרי הוא חייב בכל המצות. ואין נראה לר"י, דא"כ לא אתא לאשמועינן אלא דחייב במצות, והוה ליה למימר בהדיא דחייב במצות. ועוד, דא"כ מאי פריך ליה מברכת אבלים בעשרה, ואין אבלים מן המנין דקאמר? ברכה בשורה מי איכא? אלא ע"כ היינו ברכת המזון, והדרן קושיא לדוכתין דקתני "ואבלים מן המנין", ואוקמינן בברכת המזון. ולפירש הקונטרס לא קשיא מידי, דכי קתני "ואבלים מן המנין" היינו להצטרף לזימון, לומר "נברך שאכלנו משלו"; אבל ברכת אבלים שמברכים בברכת המזון קאמר רבי יוחנן דאינו מן המנין. לכך צריך לפרש: כי תניא ההיא בברכת המזון — היינו ברכת אבלים שבברכת המזון. מכאן משמע שברכת אבלים שבברכת המזון לא הוי אלא בעשרה, מדסליק אדעתיה דמקשן דאיירי בברכת אבלים שבברכת המזון, וקאמר בעשרה; והוה ניחא ליה בהכי, אי לאו משום דקתני לעיל בברייתא "ואבלים מן המנין", אם כן צריך עשרה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 8b:1:1.english: "When that [baraita] is taught, it is with regard to Grace after Meals" - Rashi explained in the Kuntres: [This means] to join with two others for the zimmun, since [a mourner] is obligated in all the commandments. But this does not seem right to Rabbenu Yitzchak, for if so, [the baraita] would teach us only that he is obligated in commandments, and it should have said explicitly that he is obligated in commandments. Furthermore, if so, what is the challenge [the Gemara] raises against him from "the blessing of mourners requires ten," and "mourners are not counted in the tally," which [Rabbi Yoḥanan] said? Is there a blessing in a line? Rather, of necessity it must refer to Grace after Meals, and the difficulty returns to its place, for [the baraita] teaches "and mourners are counted in the tally," and we established it as referring to Grace after Meals. According to the explanation of the Kuntres, nothing is difficult, for when [the baraita] teaches "and mourners are counted in the tally," that is to join for the zimmun, to say "Let us bless Him of whose food we have eaten"; but the blessing of mourners that is recited within Grace after Meals — about that Rabbi Yoḥanan said that [a mourner] is not counted in the tally. Therefore one must explain: "When that [baraita] is taught, it is with regard to Grace after Meals" — meaning, the blessing of mourners within Grace after Meals. From here it implies that the blessing of mourners within Grace after Meals is recited only with ten, since the questioner assumed that [the baraita] speaks of the blessing of mourners within Grace after Meals, and [Rabbi Yoḥanan] says "with ten." And this would have been satisfactory, were it not that [the baraita] taught above "and mourners are counted in the tally"; if so, ten are required.

Tosafot on Ketubot 8b:2:1.hebrew: אלא כי קאמר ר' יוחנן ברחבה - אי גרסינן "אלא", משמע דההיא דלעיל נמי מעמיד ברחבה. ותימה: למה הוצרכו תרי מילי דר' יוחנן — ההיא דלעיל והך? וצריך לומר דחדא מכלל חברתה אתמר, ההיא דלעיל מכללא דהך. אבל אי ל"ג "אלא", ניחא: דלעיל איירי בשורה, והכא ברחבה בלא פנים חדשות. ומימרא שלישית של רבי יוחנן הוצרך להשמיענו, דבפנים חדשות אין אבלים מן המנין. ואי נקט ההיא, ה"א איפכא: דוקא מיום ראשון ואילך, אבל ביום ראשון שייכי טפי, ומברכים לה בלא י':
Tosafot on Ketubot 8b:2:1.english: "Rather, when Rabbi Yoḥanan said it was in the square" - If we read "rather," this implies that the earlier statement [of Rabbi Yoḥanan] is also being explained as referring to the square. And this is puzzling: why were two statements of Rabbi Yoḥanan needed — the earlier one and this one? One must say that one was stated by implication from the other, the earlier one from this one. But if we do not read "rather," it is fine: the earlier statement deals with the line, and here [it deals] with the square, without new faces. And a third statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan was needed to teach us that with new faces, the mourners are not included in the tally. And had he stated only that one, I would have thought the opposite: [that mourners are not counted] only from the first day onward, but on the first day they are more closely connected [to the mourning], and one recites the blessing for it without ten.
